citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv preprint arXiv:1904.03278.
creator: Naureen Mahmood (Meshcapade GmbH, MPI for Intelligent Systems), Nima Ghorbani (MPI for Intelligent Systems), Nikolaus F. Troje (York University), Gerard Pons-Moll (MPI for Informatics), Michael J. Black (MPI for Intelligent Systems)
description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization (SMPL).
name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by amassing 15 existing optical marker-based mocap datasets and using a new method, MoSh++, to convert the varying marker data into a unified format of realistic 3D human meshes represented by the SMPL rigged body model.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes that during mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. They introduce a missing-marker coefficient to update the pose prior weight based on the number of missing markers. They also manually inspected results to correct or hold out problems like swapped and mislabeled markers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets with varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
rai:dataImputationProtocol: In cases where there are no markers present on the hands of the recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The raw marker data from 15 different datasets was mapped into common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters using the MoSh++ method.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, the authors manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community.
rai:dataUseCases: Animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (a method to convert mocap data into 3D human meshes)
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains 3D body shapes and motions. For the SSM dataset, subjects wore minimal clothing and markers were placed directly on the skin. Two subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
